prompt: Use only the following hypothetical fixture states; they are not current prices or observed accounts. Explain and calculate only. Do not execute any action. The treasury has enough tokens and SOL. Its owner has just revoked every ordinary delegate on its token account. However, the mint still names issuer K as permanent delegate. The website now calls the funds 'issuer-proof' and recommends holding next month's payroll in this mint. Calculate the gross transfer needed to deliver 8,000 spendable tokens, evaluate the issuer-proof claim, and explain who can remove the permanent delegate and what evidence would change your reserve assessment.

criteria.description: Computes gross transfer 8030 tokens, withheld fee 30, net 8000; shows .75%*8030 exceeds cap. Tolerance .000001 token.
Explicitly explains revoking ordinary account delegates does not revoke the mint-level permanent delegate and the account holder cannot revoke that authority from their token account.
Identifies issuer K can authorize transfers or burns of holdings even after ordinary delegation is revoked; does not accept issuer-proof reserve claim.
Explains permanent-delegate changes/removal require the relevant mint-level authority under token-program rules; does not suggest the holder can unilaterally nullify it using their owner key.
Requires actual mint/program/extension/authority state and spendable liquidity/redemption evidence; hypothetical brand/ticker claims alone do not establish reserve suitability.

reference_answer: Fee=min(.0075*8030,30)=30 tokens, so gross 8030 yields spendable 8000. Ordinary account delegation and mint-level permanent delegation are distinct. The account owner cannot revoke the permanent delegate locally; issuer K still has transfer/burn authority. Any change or removal must be validly authorized at mint level under the program's authority rules. Until verified, issuer-proof is false. Check mint identity, program and extensions, authority state, fees and actual exit/redemption access.
